newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russians confirm opposition to NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Russians confirm opposition to NATO expansion.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin and other Russian leaders confirmed their opposition to NATO's plans to expand eastwards at a top-level meeting on Monday, the Kremlin said.

Yeltsin summoned Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, presidential chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais, Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and security and defence leaders to discuss Russia's relations with the Western alliance.
"The meeting...confirmed Russia's negative position on the plans to expand NATO eastwards," Interfax news agency said, quoting Yeltsin's press secretary, Sergei Yastrzhembsky.

The dispute over NATO's plans to take in former members of the Soviet bloc looks set to dominate Russia's foreign policy in the next few months as the Western alliance prepares to issue membership invitations next July.
Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are expected to be first in line to join.
Russia says NATO's eastward expansion would threaten its security and that it would consider "adequate" measures in response.
Yeltsin had talks with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Saturday but they failed to bridge the gap between Moscow and the West over NATO's plans.

"There is a well-known divergence in Russia's position on the one hand, and Germany and the other members of the North Atlantic alliance on the other on these issues," Yastrzhembsky told Interfax on Monday.
"Boris Yeltsin clearly, precisely and fairly toughly laid out Russia's position and concern about the consequences of possible NATO expansion to the East."

Yeltsin is due to meet French President Jacques Chirac and British Prime Minister John Major soon, although dates for talks have not been announced. The dispute with NATO is likely to be one of the major items on the agenda at each meeting.
